column1:
Consistent with evidence that monetary easing can support real activity in the short run (e.g., Sims 1992; Christiano and Eichenbaum 1992), the Committee’s rate cut and ample-reserve operations are likely to bolster demand and sustain a strong labor market while inflation runs below target. At the same time, subdued market-based inflation compensation and weak business investment/exports—concerns central to inflation-targeting frameworks (Svensson)—justify the Committee’s emphasis on uncertainty and data dependence.
